column1: # v18_thrift against v12_pairs: is the throughput rate from v16 real, and is it linear downward?
# v16 added 36 instructions a row and cost 38 ms, which is the first rate this project has had:
# about 1 ms per instruction-per-row at 18 threads. Everything before it was measured as a sign,
# not a slope.
# v18 makes two changes that should test the slope from the other side. Both are pure arithmetic
# removals on the branch that hangs off `len` and never feeds back, which is exactly what the old
# latency model said could not matter: the magic-multiply digit combine (seven instructions to
# four, two multiplies to one) and the key mask taken off `trailing_zeros` instead of off the
# length derived from it (one `and` for `lsr`/`add`/`ubfiz` on the w1 side).
# The disassembly already says they do not come out as removals. Counted separately against v12's
# 214-instruction pair loop:
#                        insns/row   ubfx/ubfiz   mul   mov/movk/orr   loads
#   + magic multiply         114.5            2     6             36      26
# The arithmetic shrank as designed and the loop grew by 7.5 instructions a row, all of it
# `mov`/`movk`/`orr` rebuilding constants that no longer fit. So the prediction here is +7 ms, not
# -6, and what is really on trial is the rate: +7 means it is linear and the target has to move
# from operations to live values; near zero means v16's 38 ms was its extra load rather than its
# extra instructions.
# REPS=9 rather than 5 because a 7 ms effect sits close to the 5 ms floor the v16 batch measured.
# Each binary is entered twice under two labels. Those pairs are the batch's noise floor and
# nothing smaller than their spread may be read as a result.
v12 t18 (dup)
v18 t18 (dup)
v12 t8
v18 t8
v12 t8 (dup)
v18 t8 (dup)
